step_description: Fix COM-1 (all modules compile): make every nested example module under examples/** with its own go.mod compile cleanly, then refresh Hypergenium verifier evidence.
prompt_text:
You are working in the Lift repository. Your task is to close rubric item COM-1 (All modules compile — no ‘mystery meat’) by fixing compilation failures in nested example modules under examples/**, then re-running the deterministic Hypergenium verifier to refresh evidence under hgm-infra/.

Why this is the next step (current state)
- The latest rubric report (hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json) shows overall status FAIL, with COM-1 = FAIL.
- The COM-1 evidence log (hgm-infra/evidence/COM-1-output.log) shows failures when compiling nested example modules that have their own go.mod (multi-module repo).
- Fixing module compilation is a prerequisite for trustworthy CI enforcement (Milestone M2) and prevents drift where examples silently rot.

Hard constraints / scope control
- You MAY modify files ONLY in these areas:
  1) examples/** for the purpose of making nested example modules compile
     - Allowed file types to change: *.go (compile-only fixes like removing unused imports), go.mod, go.sum
  2) hgm-infra/** to record evidence and progress notes (and optionally update planning status).
- You MUST NOT modify any production/library code outside examples/** (do not touch pkg/**, cmd/**, internal/**).
- You MUST NOT modify the root module’s go.mod or go.sum at repo root.
- You MUST NOT modify CI/workflow files under .github/**.
- Keep changes minimal and mechanical; do not introduce new features or refactors.

Primary goal
- Make `bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh` report COM-1 as PASS.

What COM-1 checks in this repo (important)
- The verifier’s COM-1 runs a compile check for:
  - the root module
  - every nested module found via: find examples/**/go.mod
  - each nested module is compiled via: go test -run TestNonexistent -count=0 ./...
So, a single nested module with stale go.sum or a trivial build error (e.g., unused import) will fail COM-1.

Step-by-step instructions

A) Read the current failure output (no changes yet)
1) Open: hgm-infra/evidence/COM-1-output.log
2) Extract the list of failing example module directories and the exact errors.
   (Examples already observed in the log may include missing go.sum entries and an unused import in an examples/*/cdk package.)

B) Reproduce failures locally per failing module (read/execute)
For each failing module directory <moddir> (the directory containing a go.mod under examples/**):
1) Run:
   - (cd <moddir> && go test -run TestNonexistent -count=0 ./...)
2) Confirm the failure matches what’s in COM-1-output.log.

C) Fix the failures with minimal changes
Apply the smallest fix that makes the nested module compile, preferring dependency metadata fixes over code changes.

Common failure class 1: missing go.sum entry (or missing indirect requirement)
- Symptom (example): “missing go.sum entry for module providing package ... (imported by github.com/pay-theory/lift/pkg/security)”
- Fix (preferred):
  1) In the failing module directory, run:
     - go mod tidy
  2) Re-run the compile check:
     - go test -run TestNonexistent -count=0 ./...
  3) Inspect the diff and keep it minimal:
     - go.mod should not gain unrelated new direct dependencies
     - go.sum changes are expected

If go mod tidy unexpectedly upgrades many versions:
- Do NOT accept a large dependency churn as part of this step.
- Try to keep versions aligned with the root module where practical (the root go.mod is the source of version truth for the library).
- If you cannot avoid a large churn without deeper work, stop and record the problem in the notes (do not expand scope).

Common failure class 2: unused imports / trivial build errors in example code
- Example: a package imports something but doesn’t use it (Go compile error).
- Fix: make a minimal compile-only edit (e.g., remove the unused import).
- Do NOT add placeholder usage just to silence the compiler unless it is truly no-op; removing the unused import is preferred.
- Run gofmt on any modified .go files.

D) Re-run the Hypergenium verifier and refresh evidence
1) Run:
   - bash ./hgm-infra/verifiers/hgm-verify-rubric.sh
2) Confirm COM-1 is now PASS in:
   - hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json
3) Confirm the COM-1 log was refreshed and no longer contains nested module compile failures:
   - hgm-infra/evidence/COM-1-output.log

E) Record progress (required)
Create a short note file:
- hgm-infra/evidence/iterate-M2-COM-1-notes.md
Include:
- The list of example modules that were failing (paths under examples/**).
- The exact fix applied per module (e.g., “ran go mod tidy”, “removed unused import in examples/event-adapters/cdk/main.go”).
- A brief summary of what files changed (paths only; do not paste large diffs).
- The before/after status for COM-1 (FAIL → PASS) as confirmed by the updated rubric report.
- Any remaining rubric blockers from the latest report (do not fix them in this step).

F) Optional: update planning status snapshot (only within hgm-infra/planning)
If COM-1 becomes PASS, optionally update:
- hgm-infra/planning/lift-10of10-roadmap.md
so the rubric-to-milestone mapping table reflects COM-1 as PASS (use the refreshed rubric report as the source of truth).

Completion criteria
- COM-1 is PASS in hgm-infra/evidence/hgm-rubric-report.json.
- Nested example modules compile cleanly via the verifier’s multi-module compile check.
- Evidence and notes are written under hgm-infra/ (no large logs pasted into notes).

Safety / non-goals
- Do not attempt to fix maintainability budgets (MAI-1) in this step.
- Do not change lint rules/configuration or CI/workflows.
- Do not modify root go.mod/go.sum.
guardrails: Modify files outside hgm-infra/ ONLY under examples/**, and only to make nested example modules compile (go.mod/go.sum and minimal compile-only .go fixes)
Do not modify production/library code outside examples/** (do not touch pkg/**, cmd/**, internal/**)
Do not modify the root go.mod or root go.sum
Do not modify CI/workflow files under .github/**
Keep changes minimal; no refactors or feature work
Write evidence and progress notes only under hgm-infra/
Do not paste large logs into markdown notes; keep raw output in hgm-infra/evidence/*-output.log and summarize
